```{r read_in_data, echo =FALSE}
setwd("E:\\Projects\\RENEW\\Jo\\PANS\\PANS_data")
```

## Missing data

```{r missing_data, echo = FALSE}


## For all the added habitat variables, where value is NA,recoding this as 0
for (i in 614:682){
  ind<-which(is.na(pans_data[,i])==TRUE)
  pans_data[ind, i]<-0
}
rm(ind, i)

##Do this first, then replace don't knows etc with nas with custom functin
col_nums<-c(grep("M1_Q5", names(pans_data)),
            grep("M1_Q4_g", names(pans_data)),
            grep("M1_Q1", names(pans_data)), 
            grep("Wellbeing_satisfied", names(pans_data)),
            grep("Region", names(pans_data)), 
            grep("Home_IMD_Decile", names(pans_data)),
            grep("Income", names(pans_data)),
            grep("Age_Band", names(pans_data)),
            which(names(pans_data)=="Gender"),
            grep("General_Health", names(pans_data)),
            which(names(pans_data)=="Ethnicity"),
            which(names(pans_data)=="Marital_Status"),
            which(names(pans_data)=="No_Of_Vehicles"),
            which(names(pans_data)=="Interview_Date"),
            which(names(pans_data)=="Illnesses"),  grep("Dog", names(pans_data)),     which(names(pans_data)=="Work_Status"))
for (i in 1:length(col_nums)){
  ind<-grep("know|prefer", pans_data[,col_nums[i]], ignore.case = TRUE)
  pans_data[ind,col_nums[i]]<-NA
   ind<-which(pans_data[,col_nums[i]]=="")
   pans_data[ind,col_nums[i]]<-NA
}

missing_vals<-apply(pans_data[,col_nums], MARGIN = 2, FUN = function(x) sum(is.na(x))) %>%
  as.data.frame() 
names(missing_vals)[1]<-"Count"
missing_vals<-missing_vals %>%
  mutate(Percent=Count/(NROW(pans_data))*100) %>%
  mutate(Variables = rownames(.)) %>%
  as_huxtable() 
missing_vals
rm(missing_vals, col_nums, i, ind)

```

```{r create_r_modelling_index, echo = FALSE}

# Calculate modelling index with no missing values and also gender of "other" excluded

mod_ind<-which(is.na(pans_data$M1_Q5_a)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$M1_Q5_b)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$M1_Q5_c)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$M1_Q5_d)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$M1_Q5_e)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$M1_Q5_f)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$M1_Q5_g)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$M1_Q4_g)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$M1_Q1)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$Wellbeing_satisfied)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$Region)==FALSE &
                          is.na(pans_data$Home_IMD_Decile)==FALSE &
                         is.na(pans_data$Income)==FALSE &
                        is.na(pans_data$Age_Band)==FALSE &
                         is.na(pans_data$Gender)==FALSE &
                          is.na(pans_data$General_Health)==FALSE &
                            is.na(pans_data$Ethnicity)==FALSE  &
                            is.na(pans_data$Marital_Status)==FALSE  &
                            is.na(pans_data$No_Of_Vehicles)==FALSE & 
                          pans_data$Gender!="In another way (specify)" &
                            is.na(pans_data$Illnesses)==FALSE &                         is.na(pans_data$Dog)==FALSE )

mod_data<-pans_data[mod_ind,]
rm(mod_ind)
                        
                        
```



```{r rescale_weights, echo = FALSE}
subset_proportion <- nrow(mod_data) / nrow(pans_data)

# Step 2: Compute rescaled weights using the subset proportion
mod_data$rescaled_weights<-numeric(NROW(mod_data))

mod_data$rescaled_weights <- mod_data$Weight_Percent / subset_proportion

rm(subset_proportion)
```

## Q1 Outcomes

### i) Good opportunities to see nature

Q5 (M1_Q5) The next question will ask you to think about green and natural spaces close to where you live Now, thinking about green and natural spaces close to where you live, how much do you agree or disagree with the following statements? g) Provide good opportunities to see nature

### ii) Composite measure of nearby nature qualities
Supplemental Figure 1

```{r view_measure, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 7, fig.width=7, dpi = 300}

## All items about perceived qualities of nearby green and natural spaces
col_nums<-grep("M1_Q5", names(mod_data))

##convert all to factors
mod_data[,col_nums]<-lapply(mod_data[,col_nums],  function(x) as.factor(x))

mod_data[,col_nums]<-lapply(mod_data[,col_nums], function(x) factor(x, levels = c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neither agree nor disagree", "Agree", "Strongly agree")))

## Calculate count table

## up to here, something has gone wrong is it the weights?
output<-lapply(mod_data[,col_nums], function(x) as.numeric(questionr::wtd.table(x, weights =mod_data$rescaled_weights )))  %>%
  ldply(rbind) %>%
  tidyr::gather(key = "Response", value = "Counts", -.id)

output$Response<-sapply(levels(mod_data[,col_nums[1]]), FUN = function(x) rep(x,7)) %>%
  as.vector()
output$Percent<-output$Counts/(sum(mod_data$rescaled_weights))*100

names(output)[1]<-"Question"

output$Response<-factor(output$Response, levels = c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neither agree nor disagree", "Agree", "Strongly agree")) %>%
  fct_recode( 'Neither agree\nnor disagree'= "Neither agree nor disagree",  'Strongly\ndisagree'= "Strongly disagree")

output$Question<-as.factor(output$Question) %>%
  fct_recode( 'Walking distance'= "M1_Q5_a", 'Mental health and wellbeing' = "M1_Q5_b", 'High standard' = "M1_Q5_c", 'Children to play' = "M1_Q5_d", 'Physical activity and exercise' = "M1_Q5_e", 'Socialising' = "M1_Q5_f", 'Nature' = "M1_Q5_g")

## Plot distribution of each quality item
## Supplemental figure 1
p<-ggplot(output, aes(x = Response, y = Percent))+
   geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~Question, ncol = 2)+
  theme_minimal()+
  ylab("Weighted %age of respondents")+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25 , vjust = 1, hjust = 1))
p
setwd("E:\\Projects\\RENEW\\Jo\\PANS\\Figures")
ggsave("sup_fig_1_nature_qualities.png", dpi = 300, width = 7, height = 7)
rm(p, output, col_nums)


```


## Create nearby nature qualities composite
Supplemental Figure 2
```{r create_comp, echo = FALSE, fig.height=3, fig.width =4}


mod_data<- mod_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(
    starts_with("M1_Q5"),
    ~ as.numeric(.),
    .names = "{.col}_num"
  ))


col_nums_2<-grep("_num", names(mod_data))

# Chronbach's alpha
alpha_output<-psych::alpha(mod_data[,col_nums_2])
alpha_output$total
alpha_output$alpha.drop

rm(alpha_output)

## Create nature qualities composite variable
mod_data$M1_Q5_comp<-NA
mod_data$M1_Q5_comp<-rowSums(mod_data[,col_nums_2 ])
mod_data$M1_Q5_comp<-(mod_data$M1_Q5_comp/7)-3
## Check range
## It should be -2 to +2
range(mod_data$M1_Q5_comp)

rm(col_nums_2)
brks<-seq(-2, 2, 0.5)

h<-weighted.hist(mod_data$M1_Q5_comp,mod_data$rescaled_weights, breaks = brks,col=NULL,plot=FALSE)
 
h_df<-data.frame("mids" = h$mids, "counts"=h$counts)
h_df$percent<-h$counts/(sum(h$counts))*100

## Plot distribution of qualities composite
## Supplemental figure 2
p<-ggplot(h_df, aes(x = mids, y = percent))+
  geom_col() +
  xlab("Composite quality value")+
  ylab("Weighted %age of respondents")+
  theme_minimal()+
  ylim(c(0, 40))
p

setwd("E:\\Projects\\RENEW\\Jo\\PANS\\Figures")
ggsave("sup_fig_2_nearby_nature_qualities_composite_histogram.png", dpi = 300,height = 4, width = 6)

rm(brks, h, h_df,p)
```

## Create satisfaction with nearby nature opportunities variable

```{r create_binary, echo = FALSE, fig.height =3, fig.width = 6, dpi = 300}

## Explore the should and actually good opportunities to see nature variables
cross_tab<-questionr::wtd.table(mod_data$M1_Q4_g, mod_data$M1_Q5_g, useNA = "ifany", weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights) %>%
  as.data.frame() 

names(cross_tab)<-c("Should","Actually", "Freq")

cross_tab$percent<-cross_tab$Freq/(sum(cross_tab$Freq))*100

#levels(cross_tab$Should)
cross_tab$Actually<-factor(cross_tab$Actually, levels=c(rev(levels(cross_tab$Actually)[1:5]), (levels(cross_tab$Actually)[6:7])))

col_pal<-brewer.pal(5,"RdYlBu")

p<-ggplot(cross_tab, aes(x =Should, y = percent, fill= Actually))+ 
    geom_bar(position="stack", stat="identity")+
  theme_minimal()+
  scale_fill_manual(values =col_pal)+
  ylab("%age of respondents")+
  ylim(c(0, max(pretty(prop.table(table(mod_data$M1_Q4_g))*100))))+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25 , vjust = 1, hjust = 1)) 
#print as matrix/image maybe
p
rm(p, cross_tab, col_pal)

## Create satisfaction with nearby nature opportunities variable
mod_data$Nature_opp_met<-character(NROW(mod_data))
mod_data$Nature_opp_met<-NA
ind<-which((mod_data$M1_Q4_g=="Agree" | mod_data$M1_Q4_g=="Strongly agree") & (mod_data$M1_Q5_g=="Agree" | mod_data$M1_Q5_g=="Strongly agree"))  
mod_data$Nature_opp_met[ind]<-"Satisfied"

ind<-which((mod_data$M1_Q4_g=="Agree" | mod_data$M1_Q4_g=="Strongly agree") & (mod_data$M1_Q5_g=="Disagree" | mod_data$M1_Q5_g=="Strongly disagree" | mod_data$M1_Q5_g=="Neither agree nor disagree"))  
mod_data$Nature_opp_met[ind]<-"Unsatisfied"

ind<-which(mod_data$M1_Q4_g=="Disagree" | mod_data$M1_Q4_g=="Strongly disagree" | mod_data$M1_Q4_g=="Neither agree nor disagree")  
mod_data$Nature_opp_met[ind]<-"No need"

mod_data$Nature_opp_met<-as.factor(mod_data$Nature_opp_met)
#levels(mod_data$Nature_opp_met)
mod_data$Nature_opp_met<-factor(mod_data$Nature_opp_met, levels = c("Satisfied", "Unsatisfied",  "No need"))


## Explore distribution of resulting variable
tbl_nature_opp<-as.data.frame(questionr::wtd.table(mod_data$Nature_opp_met, weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights))
tbl_nature_opp$percent<-tbl_nature_opp$Freq/(sum(tbl_nature_opp$Freq))*100

p<-ggplot(tbl_nature_opp, aes(x = Var1, y = percent))+
  geom_col() +
  theme_minimal()+
  ylab("%age of respondents") +
  xlab("Nearby nature opportunities") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(pretty(tbl_nature_opp$percent)), 10), limits = c(0, max(pretty(tbl_nature_opp$percent))))
p

rm(tbl_nature_opp, ind,p)

```

## Outcomes - RQ2

### Visit frequency

```{r visit_freq, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
## Create binary visit frequency variable - visiting weekly or less often
mod_data$visit_freq_bin<-mod_data$M1_Q1 %>%
  as.factor()%>%
  fct_recode('<1 a week' = "Less often", '<1 a week' = "Once or twice a month", '>=1 a week' = "Every day",'>=1 a week' = "Twice a week", '>=1 a week' = "More than twice a week, but not every day", '>=1 a week' = "Once a week",'<1 a week' = "Never", '<1 a week' = "Once every 2-3 months")


## Explore visit frequency variables
tbl_visit_freq<-as.data.frame(prop.table(questionr::wtd.table(mod_data$M1_Q1, mod_data$visit_freq_bin, weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights))*100) %>%
  filter( Freq > 0)
tbl_visit_freq$Var2<-factor(tbl_visit_freq$Var2, levels = c("<1 a week", ">=1 a week"))

tbl_visit_freq$Var1<-factor(tbl_visit_freq$Var1, levels = c("Every day","More than twice a week, but not every day","Twice a week","Once a week", "Once or twice a month","Once every 2-3 months","Less often", "Never"))

p<-ggplot(tbl_visit_freq, aes(x=Var2,  y = Freq, fill= Var1))+
  geom_bar(position="stack", stat="identity")+
  theme_minimal()+
  ylab("%age of respondents")+
  xlab("Natural space visit frequency")+
  scale_fill_manual(values =c(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "RdYlBu"), rep("gray65",2)), name = "")+
  ylim(c(0, 80))
p
rm(tbl_visit_freq, p)

```

## Land cover

## Create land cover diversity variable

```{r num_of_lc_types_wtd_postcde, echo = FALSE}
# find the sea and estuaries/rias columns in pans data
ind_sea<-grep( "Sea_wtd|ER_wtd" , names(mod_data))

## Combine seas and estuaries/rias
mod_data$SER_wtd<-rowSums(mod_data[,ind_sea], na.rm=TRUE)
rm(ind_sea)
ind<- which(grepl("_wt", names(mod_data)) & !grepl("_B_", names(mod_data)) & !grepl("SW_wtd"  , names(mod_data)) & names(mod_data)!="Sea_wtd" & names(mod_data)!="ER_wtd" & !grepl("U_A_wtd", names(mod_data)))

num_habs_wtd<-numeric(NROW(mod_data))

# Create number of land covers variable
for (i in 1:NROW(mod_data)){
  ind_0<-which(mod_data[i,ind]>0)
  num_habs_wtd[i]<-length(ind_0)
}

mod_data$num_habs_wtd<-num_habs_wtd
rm(num_habs_wtd)

tbl_num_habs_wtd<-questionr::wtd.table(mod_data$num_habs_wtd, weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights) %>%
  as.data.frame()
tbl_num_habs_wtd$percent<-tbl_num_habs_wtd$Freq/(sum(tbl_num_habs_wtd$Freq))*100

p<-ggplot(tbl_num_habs_wtd, aes(x= Var1, y = percent))+
  geom_col()+
  theme_minimal()+
  xlab("Number of habitats")+
  ylab("%age of respondents")+
  ylim(c(0, max(pretty(tbl_num_habs_wtd$percent))))
p
rm(tbl_num_habs_wtd, ind_0,p)
rm(ind, i)
```

### Descriptive statistics - land covers
- Manuscript Table 2
- Supplemental Figure 3

```{r habs_desc, echo = FALSE, fig.width=6}

## find required land cover columns in the PANS dataset

wtd_hab_cols<-grep("wt", names(mod_data) )
wtd_hab_cols<- which(grepl("wt", names(mod_data)) & !grepl("_B_", names(mod_data)) & !grepl("Sea_wtd",  names(mod_data)) & !grepl( "ER_wtd",  names(mod_data))  & !grepl( "SW_wtd",  names(mod_data)))


## Calculate weighted descriptive statistics of the land covers for the total sample
stats_wtd_total<-apply(mod_data[wtd_hab_cols[c(1:4, 6, 18)]],
                       MARGIN = 2, FUN = function(x) c(weighted.mean(x,mod_data$rescaled_weights, na.rm = FALSE), sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x, mod_data$rescaled_weights)),wtd.quantile(x, weights=mod_data$rescaled_weights, probs=0.5), min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ldply( rbind) %>%
  mutate(wtd_habitat=c(rep("ACNG",5), rep("BMYW", 5), rep("BUAG", 5), rep("IG", 5),rep("AH", 5),rep("Count", 5)), stat = rep(c("wtd_Mean","wtd_std", "wtd_Median", "wtd_Min", "wtd_Max"), 6)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = '1') 
  
  # Calculate weighted descriptive statistics of the land covers by satisfaction with nearby nature opportunities
  
wtd_hab_names<- names(mod_data)[wtd_hab_cols[c(1:4, 6, 18)]]

stats_wtd_nat_sat <- mod_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Nature_opp_met) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(all_of( wtd_hab_names),
                                 list( wmean = ~ weighted.mean(.x, rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                       wstd = ~ sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(.x, rescaled_weights))),
                                       .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))

names(stats_wtd_nat_sat)<-gsub("_A_wtd", "", names(stats_wtd_nat_sat))
names(stats_wtd_nat_sat)<-gsub("_habs_wtd", "", names(stats_wtd_nat_sat))

tidy_stats_nat_sat <- stats_wtd_nat_sat %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer( cols = -Nature_opp_met, names_to = c("variable", "statistic"), names_sep = "_", values_to = "value" )  %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(statistic, Nature_opp_met), values_from = value) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))

rm(stats_wtd_nat_sat)

### Calculate weighted descriptive statistics  of the land covers by visit frequency
stats_wtd_visits <- mod_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(visit_freq_bin) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(all_of( wtd_hab_names),
                                 list( wmean = ~ weighted.mean(.x, rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                       wstd = ~ sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(.x, rescaled_weights))),
                                       .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))

names(stats_wtd_visits)<-gsub("_A_wtd", "", names(stats_wtd_visits))
names(stats_wtd_visits)<-gsub("_habs_wtd", "", names(stats_wtd_visits))

tidy_stats_visits <- stats_wtd_visits %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer( cols = -visit_freq_bin, names_to = c("variable", "statistic"), names_sep = "_", values_to = "value" )  %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = c(statistic, visit_freq_bin), values_from = value) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))

rm(stats_wtd_visits, wtd_hab_names)

## Categorise land covers
chop_habs<-function(habitat){
  ind<-which(habitat>0)
  ugly_cats<-chop_n(habitat[ind],round(length(ind)/4, digits = 0))
  return(table(ugly_cats))
}

  vect_cats[,i]<-cut(mod_data[[col_names[i]]], breaks = cut_brks, right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = cut_labs)
}
```

```{r hab_cats_plots, echo = FALSE}
col_ind<-c(NCOL(mod_data)-4):NCOL(mod_data)

## Calculate weighted count table for each land cover 
for (i in 1 :length(col_ind)){
  tbl_df<-data.frame(questionr::wtd.table(mod_data[,col_ind[i]], weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights))
  tbl_df$percent<-tbl_df$Freq/(sum(tbl_df$Freq))*100
  end_char<-unlist(gregexpr(pattern ='_', names(mod_data)[col_ind[i]]))[1]
  hab_name<-substr(names(mod_data)[col_ind[i]], 1, end_char-1)
  tbl_df$Habitat<-hab_name
  rm(end_char)
  assign(paste0("tbl_df_", hab_name), tbl_df)
  rm(hab_name, tbl_df)
}
```

## Sample descriptives

 Manuscript Table 1 and 2

```{r sample_descriptives, echo = FALSE}
## Manuscript Table 1
# Categorical variable names
var_names<-c("M1_Q5_g","Nature_opp_met", "visit_freq_bin","Home_IMD_quint","Income", "Region","ACNG_A_pred_ptc_wtd_percent_cats","BMYW_A_pred_ptc_wtd_percent_cats","BUAG_A_pred_ptc_wtd_percent_cats", "IG_A_pred_ptc_wtd_percent_cats","AH_A_pred_ptc_wtd_percent_cats","Age_Band", "Gender", "Ethnicity_cats", "Marital_cats", "Work_Status2", "car_cats", "Dog","Illnesses", "Gen_health_3cats",  "season","covid_restrictions", "Year")

col_nums_2<-match(var_names, names(mod_data))

variables_ordered<-names(mod_data)[col_nums_2]

## Unweighted count of each variable category
counts<-lapply(mod_data[,col_nums_2], function(x) table(x)) %>%
  ldply( rbind) %>%
  tidyr::gather(key = "Response", value = "Counts", -.id) %>%
  filter(is.na(Counts)==FALSE) %>% 
  arrange(factor(.id, levels = variables_ordered))

## Weighted percentage of each variable category in the total sample
wtd_prc<-lapply(mod_data[,col_nums_2], function(x) as.data.frame(questionr::wtd.table(x,weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights)/sum(mod_data$rescaled_weights)*100)) %>%
  ldply( rbind)  %>%
  arrange(factor(.id, levels = variables_ordered))
wtd_prc$Freq<-round(wtd_prc$Freq, digits = 2)

##  Weighted percentage of each variable category in by satisfaction with nearby nature opportunities
wtd_prc_by_need<-lapply(mod_data[,col_nums_2], function(x) prop.table(questionr::wtd.table(x,mod_data$Nature_opp_met, weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights), margin = 1)*100) %>%
  ldply( rbind) %>%
  mutate("Response"=counts$Response) %>%
  arrange(factor(.id, levels = variables_ordered))
wtd_prc_by_need[,2:4]<-round(wtd_prc_by_need[,2:4], digits = 2)


##  Weighted percentage of each variable category in by visit frequency
wtd_prc_by_vf<-lapply(mod_data[,col_nums_2], function(x) prop.table(questionr::wtd.table(x,mod_data$visit_freq_bin, weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights), margin = 1)*100)  %>%
  ldply( rbind) %>%
  mutate("Response"=counts$Response) %>%
  arrange(factor(.id, levels = variables_ordered))
wtd_prc_by_vf[,2:3]<-round(wtd_prc_by_vf[,2:3], digits = 2)

rm(variables_ordered)

## Merge all sample count and weighted percentages tables together
output_df_arranged<-data.frame(counts,"Wtd_prc"=wtd_prc$Freq, wtd_prc_by_need[,2:4], wtd_prc_by_vf[,2:3])
rm(counts,wtd_prc_by_need, wtd_prc, wtd_prc_by_vf)

names(output_df_arranged)[c(3:9)]<-c("Total_count","Total_wtd_prc", "wtd prc Satisfied","wtd prc Unsatisfied","wtd prc No need","wtd prc >=1 a week","wtd prc <1 a week")

ind<-which(output_df_arranged$Total_count>=1)
output_df_arranged<-output_df_arranged[ind,]
rm(ind)

output_flex<-flextable(output_df_arranged)

output_flex

rm(output_df_arranged,var_names,output_flex)


### numeric variables- manuscript table 2

num_vars<-c("M1_Q5_comp","Wellbeing_sat_num", "num_habs_wtd")
col_ind<-match( num_vars,names(mod_data))

# Descriptive statistics total sample
summary_table <- sapply(mod_data[,col_ind], function(x) {
  c(mean_wb = round(weighted.mean(x,w=mod_data$rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE),2),sd_w=round(sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(x, weights = mod_data$rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE)),2), median_wb = round(weighted.median(x,w = mod_data$rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE),2), min_val=min(x), max_val=max(x))
}) %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Variable") 

# Descriptive statistics by Satisfaction with nearby nature opportunities
summary_table_nat_sat <- mod_data %>%
  select(Nature_opp_met, all_of(num_vars), rescaled_weights) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = all_of(num_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Nature_opp_met, variable) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_wb = round(weighted.mean(value, w = rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    sd_w = round(sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(value, weights = rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE)), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )%>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Nature_opp_met, values_from = c(mean_wb, sd_w))

## Descriptive statistics table by visit frequency
summary_table_visit <- mod_data %>%
  select(visit_freq_bin, all_of(num_vars), rescaled_weights) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = all_of(num_vars), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(visit_freq_bin, variable) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_wb = round(weighted.mean(value, w = rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    sd_w = round(sqrt(Hmisc::wtd.var(value, weights = rescaled_weights, na.rm = TRUE)), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )%>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = visit_freq_bin, values_from = c(mean_wb, sd_w))

## Merge all descriptive statistic tables
sum_all<-merge(summary_table,summary_table_nat_sat, by.x = "Variable", by.y = "variable")
sum_all<-merge(sum_all, summary_table_visit, by.x = "Variable", by.y = "variable") %>%
  as_hux() %>%
  flextable()

print("Numeric variables")

## Print table, Manuscript table 2
sum_all

rm(summary_table, num_vars, col_ind, summary_table_nat_sat,summary_table_visit, sum_all, col_nums_2)
```

```{r multi-co, echo = FALSE}

## find predictor columns

predictor_names<-c("Region","Home_IMD_quint","Income", "Age_Band", "Marital_Status", "Gender", "Ethnicity_cats", "Work_Status2","car_cats", "Dog", "Gen_health_3cats",   "season", "covid_restrictions", "Year")
col_ind<-match(predictor_names, names(mod_data))
cors<-model.matrix(~0+., data=mod_data[, col_ind]) %>% 
  cor(use="pairwise.complete.obs") %>%
  as.data.frame()
ind_correlated<-which(cors>0.6, arr.ind = TRUE) %>%
  as.data.frame()

## Which covariates are correlated?
print("Where the numbers are the same, that represents the diagonal correlation")
ind_correlated

rm(ind_correlated, cors, col_ind, predictor_names)
```
